hints: Focus on how reactive the starting organic molecule is, especially the electron-rich C=C double bond in ethene compared to a single-bonded alcohol.
Remember the classic test for an alkene, where orange bromine water is decolourised instantly on shaking with no heating needed.
Contrast that instant electrophilic addition with the other three reactions, which all need strong heating or concentrated acid catalysts to work.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction types**

Let's look at what each equation is trying to do. A and B are additions to ethene, C is dehydration of ethanol, and D is substitution of OH by Br.

$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4 + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{Br}_2$$

**Recall the conditions for alkenes**

Alkenes are very reactive because the pi bond is exposed and electron rich. Bromine has a weak $\text{Br-Br}$ bond that is easily polarised, so electrophilic addition happens very quickly at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$ with no catalyst.

**Recall the conditions for the others**

Hydration of ethene needs steam, high temperature and pressure with $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ catalyst. Dehydration of ethanol needs hot concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ or $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$. Substitution with $\text{HBr}$ needs heating to break the strong $\text{C-O}$ bond.

**Make the deduction**

Only the addition of bromine to ethene is fast at room temperature. That is why it is used as a quick test for unsaturation in the lab.

options.A: Correct. This is electrophilic addition of $\text{Br}_2$ to the C=C bond of ethene. The pi electrons readily attack bromine, so the orange colour disappears in seconds at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$ with no heat or catalyst.
options.B: Incorrect. Hydration of ethene to ethanol, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, needs harsh conditions: steam at about $300^{\circ}\text{C}$, 60 atm pressure and concentrated phosphoric acid catalyst. Students sometimes confuse this with the easy bromine test.
options.C: Incorrect. Dehydration of ethanol to ethene is an elimination that needs strong heating with excess concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at about $170^{\circ}\text{C}$. It will not happen by just leaving ethanol at room temperature.
options.D: Incorrect. Substitution of ethanol with $\text{HBr}$ to make bromoethane needs heating under reflux. The $\text{C-OH}$ bond is strong and $\text{OH}$ is a poor leaving group, so heat is required to drive the reaction at a reasonable rate.
